slides.0.title: The north: Salta, Catamarca, La Rioja and Jujuy
slides.0.subtitle: The extreme altitudes of Cafayate and Torrontés
slides.1.title: The Calchaquí Valleys
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Extent and area
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Spanning Salta, Catamarca and Tucumán over more than 270 km, with 4,200 ha in all (Salta 3,370, Catamarca 708, Tucumán 113); the same source elsewhere gives Catamarca as 747 ha
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Altitude
slides.1.highlights.1.content: About 1,530 to 3,111 m; the town of Cafayate sits at about 1,700 m
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Climate
slides.1.highlights.2.content: About 186 mm of rain a year, concentrated in summer; in the growing season days average about 27°C and nights about 15°C, a swing of about 12°C; frost-free roughly October to April (South America Wine Guide)
slides.1.content: The Calchaquí Valleys hold some of the world's highest vineyards, starting at 1,530 m.
slides.2.title: The sub-regions of Salta
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Cafayate
slides.2.highlights.0.content: 2,518 ha, the largest sub-region; the town at about 1,700 m with some vineyards above 2,000 m; the core of Torrontés
slides.2.highlights.1.title: San Carlos, Cachi and Molinos
slides.2.highlights.1.content: San Carlos 625 ha, up to about 1,905 m; Molinos 130 ha; Cachi 87 ha, the northernmost
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Old vines and training
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Over a third of Salta's vines are more than 100 years old; about half the vineyards use VSP with drip, the rest pergola with flood irrigation
slides.2.content: Cafayate is the centre of Salta; the other sub-regions are small but higher.
slides.3.title: Tucumán, Catamarca and Jujuy
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Tucumán
slides.3.highlights.0.content: 113 ha at about 1,690–2,230 m, with about 100 mm of rain a year; Malbec is 40% of plantings and Cabernet Sauvignon and Torrontés about 17% each
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Catamarca and Jujuy
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Santa María and Fiambalá in Catamarca at about 1,700–2,200 m; the Quebrada de Humahuaca in Jujuy at about 2,200–3,329 m (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Varieties
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Torrontés, Tannat, Merlot, Syrah, Bonarda and others
slides.3.content: The further north and the higher, the varieties are still led by Malbec and Torrontés.
